identity.industry: Power electronics & energy-storage solutions (UPS / BESS / power-conditioning assembler-integrator)

summary.oneLiner: A leading India-based manufacturer of energy storage and power conditioning solutions (UPS, inverters, lithium-ion battery packs and BESS) with complementary Solar EPC, system integration and value-added services.
summary.business: Established in 2008, Prostarm Info Systems Limited designs, manufactures, assembles, sells and services a comprehensive range of power solutions under its own brand, serving commercial, industrial, institutional, government and infrastructure customers across India. Beyond its own manufactured products, the Company also sells third-party products (batteries, IT infrastructure equipment, solar panels) and provides end-to-end rooftop Solar EPC, system integration solutions and value-added services such as installation, rental, after-sales support and Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMCs).

one-line thesis: First-ever post-IPO call: net-debt-free power-electronics/BESS assembler with INR 1,202 cr order book and two new plants (Jhajjar 1.2 GWh BESS, Gujarat UPS) coming online, but a "skewed" Q4 — one Adani order (~INR 40-43 cr) slipped to Q1FY27 amid West-Asia/China supply-chain disruption — dented FY26 growth to just ~10% and ballooned receivables/working capital.
financial scorecard:
| Metric | Q4FY26 | YoY | FY26 | YoY | Notes / one-offs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Operating revenue | INR 105 cr | +27% | INR 386 cr | ~+10% | Q4 –35% QoQ; ~INR 40 cr Adani order + SAIL (INR 7 cr) + South-Eastern Railway (INR 13 cr) deferred to Q1FY27; mgmt says FY26 "could have been ~INR 430–440 cr" |
| EBITDA / margin | ~INR 11 cr / 10.43% | –3% (EBITDA) | / 12.0% | FY25 margin 12.98%, down 98 bps; cost of production 72.2%→72.78%; ~10%+ INR appreciation hit imported input cost (not fully passed on) |
| PAT / margin | ~INR 8 cr / 7.56% | +16% | ~INR 33 cr / 8.55% | FY25 PAT margin 8.24%; FY26 PAT +14% YoY |
| Order book | — | — | INR 1,202 cr | — | INR 1,106 cr executable + INR 96 cr L1; + INR 257 cr bids under evaluation |
| Working capital | — | — | INR 83 cr / 185 days | from INR 64 cr / 68 days | Debtors INR 254 cr (INR 158 cr gross tied to one Q3-executed project, collection started); FD buffer >INR 102 cr; long-term debt INR 3.4 cr→~INR 0.8 cr (net debt-free); op. cash flow ~ –INR 48 cr |
guidance (incl. next quarter):
- **FY27 revenue: minimum +25% growth.** Floor of ~INR 430 cr already visible = ~INR 330–336 cr executable order book (ex-BESS-developer) + ~INR 100 cr recurring channel business (FY26 channel did ~INR 107 cr) — before any new order wins.
- **Q1FY27 specifically:** revenue growth YoY vs Q1FY26; the deferred Q4 billings (Adani etc.) get executed in Q1/Q2. BESS order of ~INR 40 cr to be done in Q1.
- **Margins:** EBITDA 12–13% maintained on a YoY basis (base/floor "not less than 10%"); Q1/Q2 PAT margin 8.5–9.5%. Short-term interim disturbance possible.
- **Cash flow:** OCF turns positive on annual basis for FY27; visible improvement by Q3FY27.
- **Receivable days:** exit FY27 at ~120–150 days (vs 185 in FY26).
order book & pipeline:
- Executable order in hand INR 1,106 cr + L1 INR 96 cr = INR 1,202 cr; bids under evaluation INR 257 cr.
- Of ~INR 1,200 cr book, the BESS developer category (rental model, ~INR 63 cr rental/yr) is excluded from near-term revenue conversion; remaining ~INR 330–336 cr is bookable in FY27 along with ~INR 100 cr channel.
- 12-month executability: entire non-developer order book + channel = ~INR 430 cr executable within FY27.
- Notable FY26 wins: Adani, Karnataka Power, Bihar Power, L&T, West Bengal Medical, South Central Railway, SAIL, India One.
- Revenue mix: 43% government, 57% private; payment cycle same for both.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Manufacturing footprint:** 3 operational/commercialized — two in Pune (UPS & power conditioning), one Li-ion battery pack in Navi Mumbai. Two under capex (see §8).
- **Asset-light model:** not solely dependent on own factories — imports from China (customized & resold), plus job-workers for servo stabilizers, isolation transformers, and known resources for UPS. In-house used for high-end customization. Capacity therefore "not constrained."
- **EBITDA by segment not disclosed** — order-to-order, products intermingled (transformer + UPS + servo cross-sold); blended 12–13%.
- **BESS developer projects (Bihar, Karnataka):** to be hived off (in active talks with buyers); Prostarm retains the EPC portion. Project IRR ~10–11%. Bihar EPC targeted in FY27 for sure; Karnataka has legal/sub-judice hurdles.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Jhajjar 1.2 GWh BESS plant** (Haryana) — nearing commissioning, operational end of Q1FY27; revenue potential ~INR 1,000 cr (mgmt referenced INR 1,200 cr at max pace in an NDTV interview); FY27 util 25–40%, FY28 ~70%.
- **Gujarat UPS plant** (Ahmedabad, 1–600 kVA) — shifting from import/CKD assembly to SKD with more value-add; 3,000–5,000 units/day (~9 lakh units/yr) → ~INR 500–600 cr revenue potential; UPS growth >30–40% over next two years.
- Full 100% localized utilization across all facilities → ~INR 1,700–1,800 cr revenue (ex-imports).
- Tailwind: Discom-mandated BESS attached to solar plants (Maharashtra implemented, Gujarat following, some cases sub-judice) — large retrofit + new-project storage opportunity; talks ongoing with EPC players to install BESS.
- Government "ALBM" (Approved List of Battery Manufacturers) expected — seen as supportive import-substitution, not a disruption.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Q4 margin drop driven by: (a) lower-margin order mix in Q4 vs Q3; (b) employee cost up INR 22 cr→INR 29 cr (headcount 425→470) for expansion; (c) INR ~10%+ appreciation raising imported input cost, not fully passed through; (d) cost of production 72.2%→72.78%.
- China removed BESS export incentive from Apr-1 → input costs up; freight China→India >2x in Q4. New bids/sales now price-in these costs; mgmt says hit "already taken."
- Lumpy, project-led margins; blended 12–13% EBITDA defended as the through-cycle level.
capex / expansion:
- Jhajjar BESS: total capex ~INR 25 cr for ~INR 1,000 cr revenue potential (assembling, not cell manufacturing).
- Gujarat UPS: project cost ~INR 5–6 cr.
- Prior Pune Li-ion 100 MWh expansion cost only ~INR 3.5–4 cr. Asset-turn very high (mid-teens / 8–11x) because assembly-led; deeper backward integration would raise cost.
- Gujarat commissioning pushed to Q2FY27 (from Q1FY27) due to supply-chain disruptions.
capital allocation:
- Net debt-free: long-term debt INR 3.4 cr→~INR 0.8 cr. FD buffer >INR 102 cr.
- **No equity dilution planned** for FY27; ~INR 200 cr FY27 working-capital need met via internal accruals + bank lines. Promoter holding ~73% (no dilution since IPO).
- BESS developer assets to be hived off (capital-light pivot to EPC-only).
- ESOP pool 40 lakh; ~13.26 lakh outstanding as of Mar-26 + ~3.22 lakh freshly granted; more ESOPs likely for talent acquisition.
- SAP B1 + Salesforce rollout for controls/efficiency.
risks & watch-items:
- **Receivables/working-capital blow-up:** debtors INR 254 cr, WC days 185 (from 68); OCF –INR 48 cr. Heavily dependent on Q1FY27 collection of the INR 158 cr project receivable — execution risk if collections slip.
- **Concentration/lumpiness:** a single Adani order slipping caused the whole FY26 growth miss; high quarter-end (March) billing dependence.
- **Import/FX exposure:** China supply chain, freight, INR depreciation, China BESS-incentive removal — margin vulnerable; limited pass-through.
- **BESS developer hive-off execution & valuation** uncertain amid volatile lithium prices / dollar; only 10–11% project IRR.
- **Discom approval delays** for solar+BESS (Gujarat) — policy/sub-judice timing risk.
- Analyst (Archit) skepticism that FY26 underperformance vs peers is fully explained by 15-day disruption — credibility watch on Q1/Q2FY27 delivery.
management quality / tone: - Confident, granular on order book and capacity economics; candid about Q4 miss and willing to name the slipped orders (Adani, SAIL, South-Eastern Railway). Repeatedly redirected to "look at us holistically, not QoQ." Faced pointed, repeated pushback from one analyst on the peer-comparison growth gap; defended robustly (one-order-slip math) but the gap remains the central credibility test. First call post-IPO; IR via Valorem Advisors.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Despite the "1.2 GWh BESS factory" headline, this is fundamentally an **assembly/integration + import-customization** business (very high asset-turn, very low capex), not a cell/heavy-manufacturing play — capacity is rarely the constraint; working capital is.
- The "INR 1,200 cr order book" overstates near-term revenue: ~INR 63 cr/yr of it is a rental BESS-developer model being hived off; realistic FY27 base is ~INR 430 cr.
- FY26 PAT grew 14% and PAT margin improved YoY even as EBITDA margin fell — flattered by lower interest (debt repaid) and FD income, not operations.
- Channel/distribution (~INR 100 cr recurring, did INR 107 cr) is an under-discussed, non-PO base that de-risks the topline.

qoq change log:
**This quarter (Q4 & FY26 — first post-IPO call):**
- Revenue INR 105 cr (–35% QoQ, +27% YoY); FY26 INR 386 cr (+10%). EBITDA margin slid to 10.43% (Q4) / 12.0% (FY26) from 12.98% FY25.
- ~INR 40–43 cr Adani order + SAIL INR 7 cr + South-Eastern Railway INR 13 cr deferred to Q1FY27 (gas shortage for fabrication, freight, FX, China incentive cut).
- Debtors INR 254 cr, WC days 68→185, OCF –INR 48 cr; became net debt-free (LT debt INR 3.4 cr→0.8 cr); FD >INR 102 cr.
- Order book INR 1,202 cr (1,106 executable + 96 L1) + INR 257 cr bids. Decision to hive off both BESS developer projects, retain EPC.
- Gujarat plant slipped Q1→Q2FY27; Jhajjar BESS to commission end-Q1FY27.

**Next-quarter watch items:**
- Q1FY27 collection of INR 158 cr project receivable (debtor days should fall sharply) and execution of deferred Adani/SAIL/Railway billings.
- Jhajjar 1.2 GWh commissioning end-Q1FY27 and ramp to 25–40% FY27 utilization.
- Q1/Q2 revenue growth YoY and margin recovery to 12–13% EBITDA / 8.5–9.5% PAT.
- Progress on BESS developer hive-off and Bihar EPC execution.
- OCF turning positive (visible by Q3FY27); confirmation of no equity dilution.

themes.title: Renewable IPP / FDRE firm-power & storage
themes.need: DISCOMs mandating firm/round-the-clock RE make BESS + pumped-hydro the bid differentiator, and in Q1FY27 storage demand ran ahead of supply. ADANIGREEN has 3.5 GWh of BESS installed (+1.9 GWh at Khavda this quarter), targets 10+ GWh this fiscal and 50 GWh by FY30 on a thumb-rule INR 25-30 lakh of EBITDA per MWh against ~INR 1.5cr/MWh of capex, and has contracted essentially all merchant/C&I capacity to sibling AESL on 25-year (solar/wind) and 15-year (battery) fixed-price PPAs targeting ~15-16% IRR - a pivot from merchant builder to fixed-return contracted IPP, with evacuation (not panels) named as the binding constraint. JSWENERGY added 873 MW in Q1 and ~1.1 GW since April - 36% of its 3 GW FY27 target already banked, Tidong Hydro commissioned four months early - and raised INR 10,150cr, taking net leverage 5.2x to 4.95x. On the equipment side SERVOTECH said its BESS pack capacity is fully booked ('we are not able to meet the demand') and committed to 2x capacity in 6 months, 3x by 21-Mar-2027 and 10x within 2 years. ACMESOLAR/KPIGREEN/SUZLON/INOXWIND attach storage to solar/wind; NTPC/NHPC/SJVN/TATAPOWER drive pumped-hydro and utility-scale storage.
themes.driver: BESS capacity commissioning against demand two independent managements (ADANIGREEN, SERVOTECH) say already exceeds supply; FDRE/peak-power tender awards; merchant DAM prices (JSWENERGY: INR 4.40 -> INR 5.10/unit, +16%) on +8.5% Q1 power demand.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Established in 2008, Prostarm Info Systems Limited designs, manufactures, assembles, sells and services a comprehensive range of power solutions under its own brand, serving commercial, industrial, institutional, government and infrastructure customers across India. Beyond its own manufactured products, the Company also sells third-party products (batteries, IT infrastructure equipment, solar panels) and provides end-to-end rooftop Solar EPC, system integration solutions and value-added services such as installation, rental, after-sales support and Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMCs).

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Manufacturing footprint:** 3 operational/commercialized — two in Pune (UPS & power conditioning), one Li-ion battery pack in Navi Mumbai. Two under capex (see §8).
- **Asset-light model:** not solely dependent on own factories — imports from China (customized & resold), plus job-workers for servo stabilizers, isolation transformers, and known resources for UPS. In-house used for high-end customization. Capacity therefore "not constrained."
- **EBITDA by segment not disclosed** — order-to-order, products intermingled (transformer + UPS + servo cross-sold); blended 12–13%.
- **BESS developer projects (Bihar, Karnataka):** to be hived off (in active talks with buyers); Prostarm retains the EPC portion. Project IRR ~10–11%. Bihar EPC targeted in FY27 for sure; Karnataka has legal/sub-judice hurdles.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:

- **Third-Party Power Solution Products:** Batteries, IT infrastructure equipment, Solar panels, Allied power solutions
- **Solar EPC:** Rooftop Solar EPC projects
- **System Integration Solutions:** Large-scale system integration projects for enterprise and government infrastructure
- **Value-Added Services:** Installation, Rental solutions, After-sales support, Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMCs), AI-enabled remote monitoring and predictive service, QR-code-based product traceability

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
- Executable order in hand INR 1,106 cr + L1 INR 96 cr = INR 1,202 cr; bids under evaluation INR 257 cr.
- Of ~INR 1,200 cr book, the BESS developer category (rental model, ~INR 63 cr rental/yr) is excluded from near-term revenue conversion; remaining ~INR 330–336 cr is bookable in FY27 along with ~INR 100 cr channel.
- 12-month executability: entire non-developer order book + channel = ~INR 430 cr executable within FY27.
- Notable FY26 wins: Adani, Karnataka Power, Bihar Power, L&T, West Bengal Medical, South Central Railway, SAIL, India One.
- Revenue mix: 43% government, 57% private; payment cycle same for both.

guidance.title: Guidance (incl. next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **FY27 revenue: minimum +25% growth.** Floor of ~INR 430 cr already visible = ~INR 330–336 cr executable order book (ex-BESS-developer) + ~INR 100 cr recurring channel business (FY26 channel did ~INR 107 cr) — before any new order wins.
- **Q1FY27 specifically:** revenue growth YoY vs Q1FY26; the deferred Q4 billings (Adani etc.) get executed in Q1/Q2. BESS order of ~INR 40 cr to be done in Q1.
- **Margins:** EBITDA 12–13% maintained on a YoY basis (base/floor "not less than 10%"); Q1/Q2 PAT margin 8.5–9.5%. Short-term interim disturbance possible.
- **Cash flow:** OCF turns positive on annual basis for FY27; visible improvement by Q3FY27.
- **Receivable days:** exit FY27 at ~120–150 days (vs 185 in FY26).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Jhajjar 1.2 GWh BESS plant** (Haryana) — nearing commissioning, operational end of Q1FY27; revenue potential ~INR 1,000 cr (mgmt referenced INR 1,200 cr at max pace in an NDTV interview); FY27 util 25–40%, FY28 ~70%.
- **Gujarat UPS plant** (Ahmedabad, 1–600 kVA) — shifting from import/CKD assembly to SKD with more value-add; 3,000–5,000 units/day (~9 lakh units/yr) → ~INR 500–600 cr revenue potential; UPS growth >30–40% over next two years.
- Full 100% localized utilization across all facilities → ~INR 1,700–1,800 cr revenue (ex-imports).
- Tailwind: Discom-mandated BESS attached to solar plants (Maharashtra implemented, Gujarat following, some cases sub-judice) — large retrofit + new-project storage opportunity; talks ongoing with EPC players to install BESS.
- Government "ALBM" (Approved List of Battery Manufacturers) expected — seen as supportive import-substitution, not a disruption.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's BESS market is poised for strong long-term growth as energy storage becomes an essential pillar of the clean energy transition, driven by increasing renewable energy penetration, rising peak power demand and supportive government policies
- India's energy storage requirement is expected to increase from 82.4 GWh in FY27 to 411.4 GWh by FY32, with long-term demand projected to reach 2,380 GWh by 2047 (National Electricity Plan, 2023)
- India will require 888 GWh of energy storage capacity by 2035-36 (321 GWh BESS + 567 GWh pumped storage), an almost 900-fold increase over current installed capacity (India Energy Storage Alliance)
- India's UPS market is expected to see steady growth from continued digital transformation, data centre expansion, industrial automation and rising investment in critical infrastructure
- The India Power EPC / Solar EPC market is expected to see robust growth from the energy transition, expanding renewable capacity and sustained infrastructure investment, translating into a pipeline of EPC opportunities for the Company
- The India solar (hybrid) inverter market is expected to maintain strong momentum from rooftop solar adoption, favourable government schemes (National Solar Mission, PM-KUSUM, PM Surya Ghar) and rising battery-integrated solar systems
- Geopolitical developments and supply chain disruptions temporarily impacted project execution in the latter part of FY2025-26, but the underlying demand environment remains encouraging
- Increasing investments in renewable energy, energy storage, grid modernization, data centres, transportation infrastructure and industrial automation continue to create structural growth opportunities for the Company
- Revenue grew to ~Rs 386 crore in FY2025-26 with PAT up ~14%, despite higher investment in talent, manufacturing expansion and capability building; balance sheet strengthened materially post-IPO with long-term debt substantially reduced
- Healthy executable order book of over Rs 1,100 crore plus a robust bidding pipeline, providing strong revenue visibility and positioning the Company to capture emerging opportunities across India's expanding power infrastructure landscape
- Maintained strong commercial momentum by securing orders from leading organizations across the public and private sectors during FY2025-26

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- Q4 margin drop driven by: (a) lower-margin order mix in Q4 vs Q3; (b) employee cost up INR 22 cr→INR 29 cr (headcount 425→470) for expansion; (c) INR ~10%+ appreciation raising imported input cost, not fully passed through; (d) cost of production 72.2%→72.78%.
- China removed BESS export incentive from Apr-1 → input costs up; freight China→India >2x in Q4. New bids/sales now price-in these costs; mgmt says hit "already taken."
- Lumpy, project-led margins; blended 12–13% EBITDA defended as the through-cycle level.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Net debt-free: long-term debt INR 3.4 cr→~INR 0.8 cr. FD buffer >INR 102 cr.
- **No equity dilution planned** for FY27; ~INR 200 cr FY27 working-capital need met via internal accruals + bank lines. Promoter holding ~73% (no dilution since IPO).
- BESS developer assets to be hived off (capital-light pivot to EPC-only).
- ESOP pool 40 lakh; ~13.26 lakh outstanding as of Mar-26 + ~3.22 lakh freshly granted; more ESOPs likely for talent acquisition.
- SAP B1 + Salesforce rollout for controls/efficiency.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY2025-26, Prostarm progressed development of a new 1.2 GWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) manufacturing facility at Jhajjar, Haryana, and a new dedicated UPS manufacturing facility in Gujarat; both are expected to commence operations in the first half of FY2026-27, adding to the Company's existing three manufacturing facilities in Maharashtra. Within the existing footprint, the Company expanded its Bakrol, Gujarat facility to enhance standard UPS production and localisation, and strengthened its Pune facility to support customised power solutions including solar hybrid inverters and Power Conditioning Systems (PCS).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Net debt-free balance sheet supported by healthy liquidity, providing flexibility to fund growth
- Healthy, diversified executable order book (>₹1,100 crore) providing sustained revenue visibility
- Comprehensive product portfolio spanning UPS, BESS, solar solutions, power conditioning equipment and lithium-ion battery packs

- Digital and technology capabilities: AI-enabled monitoring, digital service platforms, SAP B1 and Salesforce
- Diversified presence across mission-critical sectors: healthcare, aviation, defence, BFSI, data centres, infrastructure
- Empanelled/approved vendor with multiple government agencies, strengthening public-sector credibility
- Pan-India sales and service network of 23 branch offices and 2 storage facilities across 19 states and 2 UTs

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Receivables/working-capital blow-up:** debtors INR 254 cr, WC days 185 (from 68); OCF –INR 48 cr. Heavily dependent on Q1FY27 collection of the INR 158 cr project receivable — execution risk if collections slip.
- **Concentration/lumpiness:** a single Adani order slipping caused the whole FY26 growth miss; high quarter-end (March) billing dependence.
- **Import/FX exposure:** China supply chain, freight, INR depreciation, China BESS-incentive removal — margin vulnerable; limited pass-through.
- **BESS developer hive-off execution & valuation** uncertain amid volatile lithium prices / dollar; only 10–11% project IRR.
- **Discom approval delays** for solar+BESS (Gujarat) — policy/sub-judice timing risk.
- Analyst (Archit) skepticism that FY26 underperformance vs peers is fully explained by 15-day disruption — credibility watch on Q1/Q2FY27 delivery.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Order book detail] Order in hand of INR 10,852 Mn is dominated by BESS at 8,754 INR Mn (BESS-Developer 8,538 and BESS-EPC 215), followed by Solar EPC Contracts 1,851 and Manufactured Power Solution Products 235; L1 status is 6 projects worth 50 INR Mn (UPS System).
- [Order book inconsistency] The order-book table shows Order in Hand 10,852 INR Mn plus L1 of 50 INR Mn, while the highlights text states "a robust order book, including L1 orders, of INR 10,902 Mn" — both figures are reproduced as printed, not reconciled here.
- [Listing] Listed on BSE & NSE (scrip code 544410); shareholding as on 30 June 2026 is Promoters 72.83%, Public 25.79%, DII 0.87%, FPI 0.51%; market cap INR 8,051.10 Mn at CMP 136.75 with 58.87 Mn shares outstanding.
- [BOOT/BOO model shift] The Bihar (120 MWh) and KPTCL (300 MWh) LOAs are 12-year monthly-rental developer contracts rather than EPC sales, which changes the revenue profile toward long-dated recurring rentals and implies asset ownership.
- [Marquee execution] Largest projects executed till July 2026 are integrated IT solution systems with UPS for Director General of Police, CID Pune (1,345 INR Mn) and Commissionerate of Health Services (959 INR Mn), plus SITC of UPS across 4,000+ West Bengal health centres (357 INR Mn).
